Sara —

Thanks for the note and the constraint context. Below is a commercial construct we’ve used for early-stage customers that need runway preservation while giving them meaningful term discounts and committed capacity. I’ve kept bullets short; Marissa and Vivek can follow up with final numbers and invoice language. Dev, please flag any legal constraints.

Option A — 12 month term (annual)
- 50% of contracted credits invoiced and due at signing (applies as prepaid credits).
- Remaining 50% split into 3 milestone releases (months 4, 8, 12) contingent on agreed usage gates or product milestones; credits that are not released remain refundable as cash credit on a shorter notice (we can discuss partial refunds).
- Term discount: 12% off list units (tokens/embedding unit equivalent) compared to pay-as-you-go list.
- Overage pricing: 20% above committed unit price; carry-forward up to 2 months for unused credits.

Option B — 24 month term (ramped commit)
- 40% upfront at signing; remaining 60% broken into 5 equal milestone releases every 4–5 months tied to usage or delivery milestones.
- Term discount: 20% off list units.
- Additional early-adopter credit: one-time onboarding credit of $10k in credits to help with prompt engineering and initial load testing.
- Overage pricing: 15% above committed unit price; carry-forward up to 3 months.

Commercial levers we can flex: upfront percent (40–60%), size of onboarding credit, invoice terms (Net30 vs Net45) and whether unused milestone credits convert to cash credit or are forfeited (our preference is convert-to-credit to keep things simple).

If you like, we can map exact credit volumes to your projected QPS distribution and build the Excel ramp schedule. I’ll loop in Marissa to finalize pricing and Vivek for invoice terms.

-Karthik
